of those. Newest first by default. This list only reads: a run stuck in a non-terminal state shows as `running` until its status
or result is read, which ends it.

The full result: the recommendation and every agent output, `price_band` (the code-built price band, null for a run made before it existed or with it switched off) and `business_profile` (the record the Researcher and Macro were given, null for a run made before it existed). Old runs still list the retired `tax` and `cio_stage_b` outputs among `agent_outputs`, as stored. The code-built outputs the result leaves out are on `/outputs`. 404 `ANALYSIS_NOT_FOUND`.

was not kept; 500 `BUNDLE_UNREADABLE` when the saved file cannot be read.

get.description:
What the run cost and how clean it was: wall time, model time, calls, retries, tokens, validator failures, the two gates and
the agents that left a field empty. 404 `ANALYSIS_NOT_FOUND`, or 404 `QUALITY_NOT_STORED` for a run with no summary.

Every model call of the run in the order it was made (about 44 per run): the call site, the options it ran with, its token
counts and speed, and whether its answer parsed and validated. Metadata only: the prompt and response text stay on the server.
404 `ANALYSIS_NOT_FOUND`.

What went right or wrong in the run, for a developer: a one-line verdict, the error records with a traceback tail, every
agent's status and the calls that failed. Server file paths are removed. There is no access layer on this API, so this
is meant for the owner's own machine. 404 `ANALYSIS_NOT_FOUND`.

The code-built outputs the result leaves out of `agent_outputs`, as stored: `baseline`, `consensus`, `evidence_balance`,
`stock_class`, `company_facts` and `shadow_price_band`. They feed calibration and ranking, not the CIO's words, and their keys
change with the pipeline version. A run has the ones its version built. 404 `ANALYSIS_NOT_FOUND`.

delete.description: Archives the entry and answers 204: `is_active` goes false, the change is kept in the history, and the row stays. Adding the stock again brings it back. 404 `WATCHLIST_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND`.

post.description:
What recording these rows would do: the gain or loss, the tax estimate, the room used, a superficial-loss warning
and the position after. Writes nothing. One to ten rows of one security that belong together.

Records the rows that `events/preview` shows, in one commit and answers 201. A row carrying `recommendation_id` marks that proposal followed; a stale id never fails the entry. 409 `DUPLICATE_ENTRY` for the same event within 30 seconds; 422 `INSUFFICIENT_SHARES`, `CURRENCY_MISMATCH`, `MISSING_FX_RATE`, `MISSING_CAD_AMOUNT`, `MIXED_SECURITIES` or `CONTRIBUTION_EXCEEDS_ROOM` (only for an event the system starts: a contribution the owner made over room is recorded, and the preview warns). Refused with 403 `AGENT_PORTFOLIO_READ_ONLY` for the agent portfolio.
What moving a security in kind between two accounts would do, shown for the position it leaves. Writes nothing.
Records both legs of the move under one `move_id` and answers 201. 409 `DUPLICATE_ENTRY` for the same move within 30 seconds. Refused with 403 `AGENT_PORTFOLIO_READ_ONLY` for the agent portfolio.

Undoes an entry with a correcting row; nothing is deleted. Reversing one leg of a move reverses the move. Answers 201. 404 `TRANSACTION_NOT_FOUND`; 422 `NOT_REVERSIBLE` (the row is itself a reversal, or undoing it would leave a later sale short) or `ALREADY_REVERSED`. Refused with 403 `AGENT_PORTFOLIO_READ_ONLY` for the agent portfolio.

What the correction would do: the position and the cash with the mistaken entry taken out and this one put in, and the earlier sales whose figures change. The body is the corrected entry, the same shape as one row of `events`. Writes nothing. Refuses what `correct` refuses: 404 `TRANSACTION_NOT_FOUND`; 422 `ALREADY_REVERSED` or `NOT_CORRECTABLE`.

Replaces a mistaken entry with the corrected one in one commit and answers 201 with two rows: a reversal of the original and the replacement, which points at the original (`supersedes_transaction_id`). The original stays; nothing is edited or deleted. The body is the whole corrected entry, so for a USD entry where the owner gave the rate or the Canadian-dollar amount the first time, it must be sent again (otherwise the Bank of Canada rate of the day is used). The account and the security stay the same: to change either, reverse the entry and record it again. 404 `TRANSACTION_NOT_FOUND`; 422 `ALREADY_REVERSED`; 422 `NOT_CORRECTABLE` (a reversal, one leg of a move, a detected dividend's entry, another account or security, or a correction that would leave a later sale short of shares); `CURRENCY_MISMATCH` and `MISSING_FX_RATE` as for `events`. Refused with 403 `AGENT_PORTFOLIO_READ_ONLY` for the agent portfolio.

post.summary: Remove a position entered by mistake
post.description: Reverses every entry of the holding that still counts, in one commit, and answers 201 with the reversing rows. The entries stay in the record; the holding is left with no shares. 404 `HOLDING_NOT_FOUND`; 422 `NOT_REMOVABLE` (nothing left to reverse, part of it moved in kind to or from another account, or a reversal would leave a later sale short). Refused with 403 `AGENT_PORTFOLIO_READ_ONLY` for the agent portfolio.

get.description:
Every time the owner checked the record against the broker, newest first: a position's shares or an account's cash as the record had
them (`system_value`), as the broker showed them (`broker_value`), the `difference`, and the correcting row if one was written. The
newest row of a position or account is its "last confirmed". Each one is made by `POST .../reconciliation`, which is the singular path of
this collection. Works for the agent portfolio. 404 `PORTFOLIO_NOT_FOUND`.

What is held today at the latest recorded prices, for the whole portfolio and each account. Also returns `confirmations`: for every active position and each account's cash, `last_confirmed` (empty: never), `age_days` and `overdue` (past 45 days), so a screen can say which to confirm. The agent portfolio has none.

get.summary: Read the TFSA and RRSP contribution room
get.description: The TFSA's and RRSP's contribution room rolled forward from the figure the owner entered. Shows the room today, the events since, any shortfall, and whether the figure is estimated. 422 `PROFILE_INCOMPLETE` names the profile figures it lacks.

post.summary: Reconcile a position or cash with the broker
post.description: The monthly confirm-or-correct: the shares of a position, or the cash of an account, as the broker shows them. Answers 201; a cash difference is written as an adjustment row. 422 `RECONCILIATION_DIFFERENCE` when the broker shows fewer shares than the record, or more with no cost given; `CORRECTION_NOT_VALID`. Refused with 403 `AGENT_PORTFOLIO_READ_ONLY` for the agent portfolio.

post.summary: Plan where a monthly amount should go
post.description:
Where should this money go: the split across the accounts (or the one account asked about), the RRSP year, each
account's cash to deploy, and the benchmark fund orders. Advice only. 422 `PROFILE_INCOMPLETE`, `INVALID_SURPLUS` or `INVALID_ACCOUNT`.

post.summary: Plan the cheapest way to raise cash
post.description:
The cheapest way to raise this much cash, with tax, withholding, commission, conversion and the room each source
uses. Advice only: nothing is sold. The RRSP is shown for information and never in the plan.

post.summary: Report a portfolio's profit, costs and taxes
post.description:
What the portfolio's actions earned and cost over a period, for the whole portfolio, each account and each stock,
with the actions one by one. An empty body is the current tax year to today.

post.summary: Compare two portfolios over the same dates
post.description: This portfolio beside another over the same dates (the owner's beside the agent's).

get.description:
The latest stored weekly or on-demand run (or the one named): its orders and transfers with reasons, costs and
values, what is waiting and what would release it, how far each holding sits from its target, and the report. Reads storage only; `missing` names what an older run did not keep. 404 `NO_RUN_STORED`.
One proposal with its write-up lines. 404 `PROPOSAL_NOT_FOUND`.
The run history, newest first. Filter by `kind` (weekly, adhoc or inquiry); each run counts its orders, transfers and waiting items.

post.description:
A fresh look at the portfolio, now. It is only shown unless `store` is true; saving replaces the open proposals and
the answer names them. With `allow_stale` the answer is a dry run, not a basis for orders. Answers 200, not 201, because nothing is created unless `store` is true. Refused with 403 `AGENT_PORTFOLIO_READ_ONLY` for the agent portfolio when `store` is set.

get.description: The account matrix stored with the latest run (or the one named), narrowed to a ticker or an account. 404 `NO_MATRIX_STORED` for a run stored before the matrix was kept, `NO_RUN_STORED` when there is no run.
The target book stored with the latest run (or the one named): what to hold, in which account, and why. 404 `NO_BOOK_STORED`, or `NO_RUN_STORED` when there is no run.

post.summary: Ask where an amount should go
post.description:
Where should this money go: the top three investments with their orders, or the benchmark fund when none beats it.
Nothing is sold, invested or recorded; saved as an inquiry only with `store`. Refused with 403 `AGENT_PORTFOLIO_READ_ONLY` for the agent portfolio when `store` is set.

get.description:
The dividends the portfolio was owed, oldest ex-date first: what is waiting for the owner to confirm, and what
was decided. Filter by `status` (expected, confirmed or dismissed). The system finds the dividends; no route does.

post.description:
What confirming would do, with any corrections: the cash, the position after, and a warning for a probable
duplicate. Writes nothing. 404 `DIVIDEND_EVENT_NOT_FOUND`.

Accepts the calculated dividend, or corrects it, and records it (with its reinvestment for an account that
reinvests) in one commit and answers 201; the decision is in the history (`GET /api/history`). Refused once decided, before the payment date, or with no shares at the ex-date. 409 `EVENT_NOT_OPEN` once decided, 409 `NOT_PAID_YET` before the payment date, 422 `NO_SHARES_AT_EX`, `NO_REINVESTMENT_PRICE` or `INVALID_CORRECTION`. Refused with 403 `AGENT_PORTFOLIO_READ_ONLY` for the agent portfolio.

The dividend was not received, or is already in the record. It is not found again unless it is reopened (`POST .../reopen`); the decision is in the history. 409 `EVENT_NOT_OPEN` once decided. Refused with 403 `AGENT_PORTFOLIO_READ_ONLY` for the agent portfolio.

Takes a decision back so the dividend can be decided again. A dismissed dividend becomes expected; a confirmed one first has its dividend and reinvestment entries reversed (they stay in the record) and then becomes expected, in one commit. Each change of status is in the history (`GET /api/history`). 409 `EVENT_NOT_DECIDED` when the dividend is still expected; 422 `NOT_REVERSIBLE` when reversing would leave a later sale short of shares. Refused with 403 `AGENT_PORTFOLIO_READ_ONLY` for the agent portfolio.

get.description:
One prediction per analysis, newest first: the tier and the return range the price band gave, the call it came from, the
four checkpoints (1, 3, 6 and 12 months) with what happened once each is resolved, and the shadow CIO's call on the same run.
A prediction made without a price band has no tier or range and no checkpoints. Checkpoints are `pending` until the closing
price is in; only a resolved one has outcomes. Only columns that are written are returned: the stored scores and the
accuracy and cost estimates are never filled, so they are not here.

get.description:
The versions declared in `pipeline_versions.json`, oldest first (the latest is the last): the prompts hash, band settings
and model each was declared with, what changed, and whether its view is comparable with the previous version's. A run
records its version in its result. 500 `PIPELINE_REGISTRY_UNREADABLE` when the registry file cannot be read.

The monthly feedback scorecard as the scheduled job saved it: whether the CIO's calls ranked stocks the right way against the
market (Q1), whether the band moved its target by the right amount (Q2), whether repeated runs agree, the problems found and the
decision-log follow-ups. It is as of the day it was made for, so it is only as fresh as the last monthly run (the script
`scripts/feedback_scorecard.py` writes a new one). `page` (the default) is the readable page the owner reads, as `{markdown}`;
`overview` is the small keys (counts, thresholds, problem lists, the pipeline registry); `scoring`, `descriptive`,
`consistency` and `baseline` are those parts of the report unchanged, each figure with an id that `/figures/{figure_id}` traces
to its rows. A scorecard from an older scorer may lack a part, which then comes back empty. The scoring set is empty until
batch runs of the current cohort resolve. 404 `SCORECARD_NOT_FOUND`.

get.summary: Trace a scorecard figure to its rows
get.description:
One figure of the saved scorecard by its exact id (`<set>.<cohort>.<horizon>.<measure>`, for example
`descriptive.pooled.1m.q1.rank_correlation`; `current` stands for the scoring set's current cohort) and the rows it rests on:
each run at that horizon with its call, band and outcome, largest outcome first. A consistency figure rests on repeated calls,
not outcomes, so it has no rows; a baseline figure has rows only when the scorecard saved its baseline observations.
404 `SCORECARD_NOT_FOUND`, or 404 `FIGURE_NOT_FOUND` when the scorecard has no such figure.

get.summary: Read the optimizer's view of a stock
get.description:
What the optimizer reads about a stock: the newest completed `medium_term` analysis, its price band rebuilt at the latest stored price,
the CIO's words, the class and labels, and every reason the stock is excluded (`exclusions`; `rerun_reasons` is the part a new analysis would
fix). A stock with no usable analysis, or one the pipeline cannot analyse, answers 200 with `status: excluded`. 404 `STOCK_NOT_FOUND`.

The benchmark fund's newest stored record (its band with no view, the fee, the income, the Bank of Canada rate used; `stale` when over a
week old) and its contents (the largest holdings and the part of the fund they cover; `stale` when over 35 days old). The funds are the
listings the market line is drawn from (`VFV.TO`, `VOO`). 404 `FUND_NOT_FOUND` for any other ticker, or a fund with no record stored yet.

The Bank of Canada USD/CAD observations (Canadian dollars per US dollar) from `from` to `to`, oldest first; the Bank publishes on business
days only. They are fetched from the Bank on every request, through the request's provider scope, and not stored. 422 `INVALID_DATE_RANGE`
when `from` is after `to` or the range is over 400 days; 503 `EXCHANGE_RATE_UNAVAILABLE` when the Bank cannot be reached or answers nothing usable.

correlate above 0.7, which count as one. Values use the stored prices and, for US holdings, the Bank of Canada rate; a missing rate or a
short history is a `warnings` entry, not an error. `as_of` defaults to today (Toronto). Works for the owner's portfolio and the agent's.
404 `PORTFOLIO_NOT_FOUND`.

out the stack trace, the context and the resolution notes; `GET /api/errors/{error_id}` has them. Read only: no error is ever acknowledged or
resolved through the API yet, so `status` is `open` throughout.

get.summary: Read how the weekly batch stands
get.description:
One scored analysis of every stock on the batch list each week, a few each weekday morning. This says who is done, pending or given up this
week (`week`), which stocks are due on `as_of` (default today, Toronto; `due_today`, at most 8, the cap for one morning, most overdue first;
`week.pending` lists everything still open) and the list itself. The list is the file `backend/batch_list.json`, outside the database.
503 `BATCH_LIST_UNAVAILABLE` when it cannot be read or is not valid.

Whether the database is at the head of its migrations (`database.migrated`) and which settings an analysis needs and the server lacks, by
variable name and never by value (`providers`), for a Canadian stock, a Canadian stock also listed in the US, and a US stock. `status` is `ok`
or `degraded`; the answer is always 200, since the body is the answer. The model server is not checked: only the agents may reach it.

get.summary: List the changes made to one thing
get.description:
Every field of the thing that was changed through the API, newest first: the old value, the new one, who changed it
(`owner`, or `system` for what a job did) and when. An edit never loses its old value; this is where it is kept. A dividend's
confirm, dismiss and reopen are changes of its `status`. A thing that was never changed has an empty list, whether or not it
exists.

AlternativeViewResponse.description: An option the run did not take, and why: the next stock the cash could have gone to, or "keep it" for a sale.

AnalysisFailure.title: AnalysisFailure
AnalysisFailure.description:
Why a run failed, for a caller that sees status "failed" (86bc997wr).

Deliberately small and sanitized: the stage it stopped at and a short,
credential-redacted reason. Never a traceback, a file path, or model output;
the full picture (traceback tail, evidence files) is in
error_records and is read through GET /api/analysis/{id}/diagnosis (paths removed) and scripts/diagnose_run.py.

price_band.title: Price Band
price_band.description: The code-built price band: a record with status `ok` (current_price, range, slider, target_price, expected_total_return_pct, by_horizon, risk_profile and more) or `unavailable` with a reason. Null on runs made before the band existed or with it switched off. Keys: docs/technical/price-band-design.md section 6.

business_profile.title: Business Profile
business_profile.description: The business profile record the Researcher and Macro were given (status `ok`, `none` or `failed`): identity, classification, series, economics, gaps and meta. Null for runs made without one. Keys: docs/technical/business-profile-design.md section 3.

timeline.title: Timeline
timeline.description: `short_term` or `medium_term`; one old stored run carries a retired timeline value.

duration_s.title: Duration S
duration_s.description: Seconds from the request to completion; null until the run completes.

pipeline_version.title: Pipeline Version
pipeline_version.description: The pipeline version the run recorded (`P17` and so on). Null on runs made before versions were recorded.

timeline.title: Timeline
timeline.description: `short_term` or `medium_term`; one old stored run carries a retired timeline value.

stock_outlook_direction.title: Stock Outlook Direction
stock_outlook_direction.description: Null for a run that failed before the CIO.

AnalysisRunSummary.title: AnalysisRunSummary
AnalysisRunSummary.description: One run in the history: who and when, how it ended, and the call it made.

AskCreate.title: AskCreate
AskCreate.description:
Where should this money go: the top three investments with their orders. Saved as an inquiry only when `store` is
true; an inquiry never replaces a run and is never mirrored to the agent portfolio.

settings_version.title: Settings Version
settings_version.description: `B1`, `B2` and so on: the baseline's settings the fit was made under.

usd_cad.title: Usd Cad
usd_cad.description: The rate US-dollar earnings were converted at for Canadian listings.

usable_count.title: Usable Count
usable_count.description: Stocks whose record could be turned into features.

fit.title: Fit
fit.description: The fitted model, as `data.precompute.baseline.Fit.to_json()` wrote it.

drift.title: Drift
drift.description: How the gaps moved since the previous fit; null for the first fit.

BaselineFitResponse.title: BaselineFitResponse
BaselineFitResponse.description: One weekly fit of the baseline over the reference universe (about 720 stocks).

market_return_pct.title: Market Return Pct
market_return_pct.description: Its market fund, the same way.

required_pct.title: Required Pct
required_pct.description: The required return over the horizon: the risk-free rate plus shrunk beta times the equity premium.

flat_pct.title: Flat Pct
flat_pct.description: The risk-free rate plus the equity premium over the horizon.

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: Beta, rate day, flags, resolver and settings versions.

BaselineOutcomeResponse.title: BaselineOutcomeResponse
BaselineOutcomeResponse.description: What the market did after one stock's baseline, at one horizon: facts only; the scorer makes every comparison.

outcomes.title: Outcomes
outcomes.description: Empty until a horizon falls due and is resolved.

BaselineUniverseRowResponse.title: BaselineUniverseRowResponse
BaselineUniverseRowResponse.description:
One stock's baseline in one fit: the record the baseline produced (its inputs, every model's gap, the revision and the edge)
and the outcomes that have come in.

weekday.title: Weekday
weekday.description: 0 (Monday) to 4 (Friday): the day its weekly analysis is due.

removed.title: Removed
removed.description: Set once it is taken off the list; its history stays.

BatchStockResponse.title: BatchStockResponse
BatchStockResponse.description: One stock on the batch list.

required.title: Required
required.description: Stocks active at the start of the week: the week is complete when each is done, given up or removed.

done.title: Done
done.description: Stocks with a scorable run this week.

gave_up.title: Gave Up
gave_up.description: Stocks that used all their counted attempts without a scorable run.

pending.title: Pending
pending.description: Active stocks not done and not given up, everything still open.

BatchWeekResponse.title: BatchWeekResponse
BatchWeekResponse.description: Who is done, pending or given up this week, from `services/weekly_batch.week_status`.

BenchmarkLineResponse.title: BenchmarkLineResponse
BenchmarkLineResponse.description: What the benchmark fund earns in an account after costs: the line a stock is measured against.

field.title: Field
field.description: The field that changed; a dividend decision is a change of `status`.

old_value.title: Old Value
old_value.description: The value before, in JSON form.

new_value.title: New Value
new_value.description: The value after, in JSON form.

ChangeResponse.title: ChangeResponse
ChangeResponse.description: One field that changed: what it held, what it holds now, who changed it and when.

ComparisonRequest.title: ComparisonRequest
ComparisonRequest.description:
The other portfolio to set beside the one in the path (the owner's beside the agent's), and the period and scope
both are reported over.

ConfirmationResponse.title: ConfirmationResponse
ConfirmationResponse.description:
When a position or an account's cash was last checked against the broker. Past 45 days it is overdue: the monthly
plan warns about it and makes no plan from it.

migrated.title: Migrated
migrated.description: The database is at the head of the migrations.

revision.title: Revision
revision.description: The revision the database holds; null when it has no `alembic_version` table.

heads.title: Heads
heads.description: The head revision of the migration scripts (more than one means branches).

DiagnosisResponse.title: DiagnosisResponse
DiagnosisResponse.description:
Everything known about why one run went the way it did (`services/error_report.diagnose_run`), for a developer: the
verdict, the error records with a traceback tail, every agent's status and the failing calls. Local file paths are removed.

DividendConfirmedResponse.title: DividendConfirmedResponse
DividendConfirmedResponse.description:
What confirming recorded: the event as decided, the rows written (the dividend, then the reinvestment when the
account reinvests) and anything worth knowing, such as a probable duplicate.

gross.title: Gross
gross.description: the dividend received, before tax withheld

reinvest.title: Reinvest
reinvest.description: override the account's setting for this dividend

DividendCorrections.title: DividendCorrections
DividendCorrections.description:
What the owner changes when the broker's figures differ from the calculated ones. Anything left out keeps the
calculated figure; a corrected gross with no withholding given re-works the withholding at the same rate.

DividendDismiss.title: DividendDismiss
DividendDismiss.description: The dividend was not received, or is already in the record. Final: it is not found again.

run_id.title: Run Id
run_id.description: The analysis it happened in, when it was in one.

status.title: Status
status.description: `open`, `acknowledged`, `investigating`, `resolved`, `auto_fixed` or `wont_fix`. Nothing changes it yet: every error is `open`.

stack_trace.title: Stack Trace
stack_trace.description: With the server's folders removed from every path.

context_json.title: Context Json
context_json.description: What the system knew when it recorded the error, with the server's folders removed from any path.

ErrorDetailResponse.title: ErrorDetailResponse
ErrorDetailResponse.description: One error in full: the stack trace and the context (server paths removed), and the resolution fields.

run_id.title: Run Id
run_id.description: The analysis it happened in, when it was in one.

status.title: Status
status.description: `open`, `acknowledged`, `investigating`, `resolved`, `auto_fixed` or `wont_fix`. Nothing changes it yet: every error is `open`.

ErrorSummaryResponse.title: ErrorSummaryResponse
ErrorSummaryResponse.description: One error as the list shows it. Equal errors are one row with an `occurrence_count`.

EventPreviewResponse.title: EventPreviewResponse
EventPreviewResponse.description: What recording the body would do. Nothing was written.

EventsCreate.title: EventsCreate
EventsCreate.description: One or several rows that belong together, all of one security (a dividend with the reinvestment that spends it).

rate.title: Rate
rate.description: Canadian dollars for one US dollar.

weight.title: Weight
weight.description: The combined share of the names the portfolio holds.

ExposureGroupResponse.title: ExposureGroupResponse
ExposureGroupResponse.description: Names that correlate above 0.7 with each other, counted as one.

direct.title: Direct
direct.description: A share of the portfolio's total value held directly.

via_funds.title: Via Funds
via_funds.description: A share held inside funds, from the funds' largest holdings.

group.title: Group
group.description: The correlated group it belongs to, when the group has more than one name.

ExposureNameResponse.title: ExposureNameResponse
ExposureNameResponse.description: One company, however it is listed (RY and RY.TO are one), with what the portfolio holds of it directly and through funds.

ExposurePairResponse.title: ExposurePairResponse
ExposurePairResponse.description: The weekly-return correlation of two names (a pair just below the group threshold, or any pair of the correlation table).

cash.title: Cash
cash.description: Cash as a share of the total.

not_itemised.title: Not Itemised
not_itemised.description: The share of fund holdings the sources do not itemise.

held_both_ways.title: Held Both Ways
held_both_ways.description: Names held directly and inside a fund.

near_misses.title: Near Misses
near_misses.description: Pairs just under the group threshold.

benchmark_vol.title: Benchmark Vol
benchmark_vol.description: The benchmark's own volatility over the same window.

usd_cad.title: Usd Cad
usd_cad.description: The rate US-dollar holdings were valued at.

ExposureResponse.title: ExposureResponse
ExposureResponse.description:
What a portfolio holds counting what its funds hold, by sector, industry and currency, with the risk of each name and the correlated
groups. Shares are fractions of `total_value_cad`.

vol_quote.title: Vol Quote
vol_quote.description: The same in the stock's own currency.

beta.title: Beta
beta.description: To the benchmark, in Canadian dollars.

resid_vol.title: Resid Vol
resid_vol.description: Annualised volatility the benchmark does not explain.

flags.title: Flags
flags.description: For example a history too short to trust.

ExposureRiskResponse.title: ExposureRiskResponse
ExposureRiskResponse.description: The risk of one stock from a year of weekly Canadian-dollar returns.

FalsifierResponse.title: FalsifierResponse
FalsifierResponse.description: The price that would end the trend behind the call (the CIO's `technical_trigger`).

coverage.title: Coverage
coverage.description: The part of the fund the listed holdings account for, at most 1.

FundContentsResponse.title: FundContentsResponse
FundContentsResponse.description: What the fund held, as far as the source says: its largest holdings (about the top ten).

record.title: Record
record.description: The fund's record as `core_funds.build_fund_record` wrote it (a band built with no view, the fee, the income, the rate used), plus `stale`.

contents.description: Null when no contents are stored for the fund.

FundResponse.title: FundResponse
FundResponse.description: A benchmark fund: its latest stored record and its contents.

status.title: Status
status.description: `ok`, or `degraded` when the database is behind its migrations or a setting is missing.

HiddenOutputResponse.title: HiddenOutputResponse
HiddenOutputResponse.description: A code-built output of a run that is left out of the result's `agent_outputs`, as stored.

run_id.title: Run Id
run_id.description: The analysis the view rests on; null when there is none.

exclusions.title: Exclusions
exclusions.description: Every reason the stock is excluded; empty when usable.

rerun_reasons.title: Rerun Reasons
rerun_reasons.description: The part of `exclusions` a new analysis would fix.

price.title: Price
price.description: The live price, in the quote currency.

expected_total_return.title: Expected Total Return
expected_total_return.description: A fraction over the band's horizon, in the quote currency.

market_reference.title: Market Reference
market_reference.description: The flat market baseline, a fraction.

view_points.title: View Points
view_points.description: The CIO's view, in percentage points.

view_noise_points.title: View Noise Points
view_noise_points.description: What one tier step of the label moves the prediction by, in percentage points.

view_history_weeks.title: View History Weeks
view_history_weeks.description: Weekly views behind the view, at most 4.

view_jump_steps.title: View Jump Steps
view_jump_steps.description: The change in the latest weekly reading since the one before, in tier steps.

view_unstable.title: View Unstable
view_unstable.description: Whether the view reversed in the last three weeks.

valuation_edge.title: Valuation Edge
valuation_edge.description: The stock's edge over its required return, a fraction over the band's horizon; 0 when it is not valued.

InstrumentViewResponse.title: InstrumentViewResponse
InstrumentViewResponse.description:
The optimizer's view of one stock (`services/instrument_view.py`): its newest completed `medium_term` analysis, the band rebuilt at
the live price, and every reason it is out of buys and view-driven sells. Returns are fractions; `view_points` and
`view_noise_points` are percentage points.

LlmCallResponse.title: LlmCallResponse
LlmCallResponse.description:
One model call of a run: which call, the options it ran with, its size and speed, and whether its answer parsed and
validated. Metadata only: the prompt and response text stay in files on the server and are never returned.

MonthlyPlanRequest.title: MonthlyPlanRequest
MonthlyPlanRequest.description:
"I have this much to invest." The amount may be zero (the plan then shows the year as it stands); an amount below
zero is refused by the service (INVALID_SURPLUS). With `account` the whole amount is for that account only.

MonthlyPlanResponse.title: MonthlyPlanResponse
MonthlyPlanResponse.description: The answer to "I have this much to invest". Advice only: nothing in it is invested or recorded.

MoveCreate.title: MoveCreate
MoveCreate.description:
A security moved in kind from one account to another (design 5.15): the shares leave one account and arrive in
the other, with no cash. The price is the market price on the day, because the move is valued there: out of Trading
it is a sale at that price (a gain is taxed, a loss is nil), into Trading it sets the new cost. Recorded as two
rows that share a `move_id` (`legs`).

OrderViewResponse.title: OrderViewResponse
OrderViewResponse.description: One step of a run: an order to place, or a transfer between the owner's own accounts.

PipelineVersionResponse.title: PipelineVersionResponse
PipelineVersionResponse.description:
One declared version of the pipeline (`backend/pipeline_versions.json`): the prompts and band settings a run was made
under.

PositionAfterResponse.title: PositionAfterResponse
PositionAfterResponse.description: The position an event leaves, in the stock's currency and in Canadian dollars (the tax cost base).

PositionsResponse.title: PositionsResponse
PositionsResponse.description:
What the portfolio holds today, valued at the latest recorded prices: positions with value, CAD cost base,
unrealised gain and weight, and cash. Whole portfolio and each account.

PredictedLinesResponse.title: PredictedLinesResponse
PredictedLinesResponse.description:
The predicted-return lines of the name and account an order is in, from the account matrix stored with the run.
Returns, rates and costs are fractions (0.0797 is 7.97%); `noise_margin_pts` and `tax_rate_pct` are points.

status_reason.title: Status Reason
status_reason.description: Why a pending or needs-review checkpoint is waiting.

actual_total_return_pct.title: Actual Total Return Pct
actual_total_return_pct.description: Price change plus dividends, over the price at the call.

excess_return_pct.title: Excess Return Pct
excess_return_pct.description: The stock's total return minus the benchmark's.

interpolated_expected.title: Interpolated Expected
interpolated_expected.description: The return the band expected by this date.

exit_date.title: Exit Date
exit_date.description: The trading day whose close was used.

resolution_detail.title: Resolution Detail
resolution_detail.description: Every input the resolver used, so the outcome can be recomputed.

PredictionCheckpointResponse.title: PredictionCheckpointResponse
PredictionCheckpointResponse.description:
One look at a prediction against what happened: due at 1, 3, 6 or 12 months. A checkpoint is `pending` until its closing
price is in; only a `resolved` one has the outcome fields.

stock_outlook_direction.title: Stock Outlook Direction
stock_outlook_direction.description: The CIO's outlook on the run the prediction came from.

checkpoints.title: Checkpoints
checkpoints.description: Oldest due date first; empty when no band was made.

PredictionResponse.title: PredictionResponse
PredictionResponse.description:
What the CIO's call was expected to return, with the outcomes that have come in. A prediction made without a price band
has no tier or range and no checkpoints.

PriceResponse.title: PriceResponse
PriceResponse.description: One trading day's stored prices, in the stock's own currency.

ProposalRunCreate.title: ProposalRunCreate
ProposalRunCreate.description:
Ask for a fresh look at the portfolio. Nothing is saved unless `store` is true, and saving replaces the portfolio's open
proposals (their ids are listed in the answer). `allow_stale` weights a name whose only fault is an analysis over a week
old; the answer is then marked a dry run.

canadian_crosslisted_missing.title: Canadian Crosslisted Missing
canadian_crosslisted_missing.description: For a Canadian stock also listed in the US (its SEC filings).

ProviderHealth.title: ProviderHealth
ProviderHealth.description: The settings an analysis needs and the server lacks, by variable name. Never a value.

RaiseCashRequest.title: RaiseCashRequest
RaiseCashRequest.description: How much cash is needed in hand.

RaiseCashResponse.title: RaiseCashResponse
RaiseCashResponse.description: The cheapest way to raise cash. Advice only: nothing in it is sold, recorded or created.

RaiseOptionResponse.title: RaiseOptionResponse
RaiseOptionResponse.description: One way to raise cash. A sale is whole shares; `net_cad` is what reaches the owner's hands.

ReconcileCash.title: ReconcileCash
ReconcileCash.description: The cash the broker shows in an account, in both currencies; a difference is written as an adjustment row.

ReconcilePosition.title: ReconcilePosition
ReconcilePosition.description:
The shares the broker shows for one position. More at the broker with the cost of the missing shares given closes
the difference; fewer needs the sale or transfer that explains them (nothing is guessed).

RecordedEventsResponse.title: RecordedEventsResponse
RecordedEventsResponse.description: The rows an entry or a reversal wrote, in the order they were written.

ReportResponse.title: ReportResponse
ReportResponse.description:
What a portfolio's actions earned and cost over a period: the total, each account, each stock, who did what and why,
the breakdowns asked for and the actions one by one. Information only; nothing in it is recorded or scored.

ReportSpec.title: ReportSpec
ReportSpec.description: What to report on. Nothing set means the current tax year to today, for every account and stock.

RunQualityResponse.title: RunQualityResponse
RunQualityResponse.description: What one run cost and how clean it was: time, calls, tokens, validator trouble and the two gates.

figure.title: Figure
figure.description: The figure: its id, set, cohort, horizon, value, how many observations and blocks it rests on, and whether that is too few.

ScorecardFigureResponse.title: ScorecardFigureResponse
ScorecardFigureResponse.description: One figure of the scorecard and the rows behind it, largest outcome first.

as_of.title: As Of
as_of.description: The day the scorecard was made for; the data is as of this day.

available.title: Available
available.description: Every saved scorecard, newest first; pick one with `as_of`.

ScorecardResponse.title: ScorecardResponse
ScorecardResponse.description:
One part of a saved monthly scorecard. `data` is that part of the report as the scorer wrote it (its structure is in
docs/technical/feedback-engine-design.md, sections 5.8 and 5.9), or `{"markdown": ...}` for the readable page.

primary_cio_outlook_distance.title: Primary Cio Outlook Distance
primary_cio_outlook_distance.description: Steps apart on the five-point outlook scale, 0 to 4.

high_divergence.title: High Divergence
high_divergence.description: True when the two outlooks are more than two steps apart.

ShadowPredictionResponse.title: ShadowPredictionResponse
ShadowPredictionResponse.description: The shadow CIO's call on the same run: what it said beside the primary CIO, and how far apart they were.

stock_id.title: Stock Id
stock_id.description: Null for a ticker the database has not seen.

currency.title: Currency
currency.description: The currency the stock trades in.

instrument_type.title: Instrument Type
instrument_type.description: `equity`, `etf` or `other`; null for a row that never recorded one (an equity the pipeline already served).

pipeline_supported.title: Pipeline Supported
pipeline_supported.description: Whether the analysis pipeline can serve it. An unsupported instrument can still be held; it is never analysed or traded by the optimizer.

source.title: Source
source.description: `database` when the stock is already known (no provider was asked), `provider` when the data providers answered.

StockLookupResponse.title: StockLookupResponse
StockLookupResponse.description:
What the system can say about a ticker before it is added to a portfolio or a watchlist: a stock row, plus where the answer came from.
Nothing is recorded.

currency.title: Currency
currency.description: The currency the stock trades in.

instrument_type.title: Instrument Type
instrument_type.description: `equity`, `etf` or `other`; null for a row that never recorded one (an equity the pipeline already served).

pipeline_supported.title: Pipeline Supported
pipeline_supported.description: Whether the analysis pipeline can serve it. An unsupported instrument can still be held; it is never analysed or traded by the optimizer.

StockResponse.title: StockResponse
StockResponse.description: A stock the system knows: one row of the directory.

TargetBookResponse.title: TargetBookResponse
TargetBookResponse.description: What to hold and where, and the reason for each choice. The decision rules compare it with what is held.

TransactionCreate.title: TransactionCreate
TransactionCreate.description:
One event for the record, as the broker reports it. Used by the event processor (`insert_transaction`,
`preview_event`) and the seed script; no route writes it yet (the event route comes with ticket 9). Shares are
signed the way they are stored: negative for a sell or transfer out. For a USD row the processor fills the CAD
figures from the Bank of Canada rate of the date unless the owner gives a rate or a CAD amount. A dividend's date
is the day the cash arrived.

ViewNoteResponse.title: ViewNoteResponse
ViewNoteResponse.description: The CIO's words and labels for a name, kept with the run. For information only.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The profile the batch's analyses are made for.

due_today.title: Due Today
due_today.description: The stocks to analyse today, most overdue first, at most 8 (the batch's cap for one morning); `week.pending` lists all that are still open.

stocks.title: Stocks
stocks.description: Every stock on the list, removed ones included.

WeeklyBatchResponse.title: WeeklyBatchResponse
WeeklyBatchResponse.description: How the weekly batch stands: the week's progress, what is due today and the list itself.
